samples.text:
The pie charts shows the reasons of international visitors for coming to one country in 2014 and 2024.

In 2014, holiday was the most common reason with 44% of visitors. Business was the second reason, it was 28%, and visiting friends or relatives was 18%. Study and other reasons was both 5%. It means that holiday and business together was the reason for most of the visitors in 2014.

In 2024, holiday was still the main reason and it increased to 51%, so more than half visitors came for holiday. Business decreased a lot to 14%, which is half of 2014. Visiting friends and relatives increase a little to 21% and it became the second reason. Study also increased, it doubled from 5% to 10%. Other reasons went down slightly to 4%.

Overall, holiday was the main reason in both years. The biggest change was business which fell very much, while study and holiday became more popular than before. Visiting friends and relatives was also a bit more popular in 2024.
samples.why: Accurate figures covering all categories · overview only at the end · simple, repetitive linking and vocabulary · several agreement, preposition and tense errors that do not obscure meaning.

samples.text:
The pie charts illustrate the main purposes of international visitors travelling to one country in 2014 and 2024.

Overall, holidays were the most common reason for visiting the country in both years, and their share rose over the decade. The most significant change was the sharp fall in business travel, while the proportion of students doubled.

In 2014, 44% of visitors came on holiday, and business trips accounted for just over a quarter (28%). Visiting friends and relatives was the third most common purpose, at 18%, whereas study and other reasons each represented only 5% of visitors.

By 2024, holidaymakers made up more than half of all visitors (51%). In contrast, the share of business travellers halved, falling to 14%, which meant that visiting friends and relatives (21%) overtook business as the second most important reason. The number of people coming to study also increased noticeably, from 5% to 10%. Finally, the percentage of visitors travelling for other reasons remained almost unchanged, dipping slightly to 4%, so it was still the least common purpose of all.
samples.why: Clear overview of the main changes · key features well highlighted and accurately supported · logical paragraphing · range of linkers with slight over-use of sequencing · one minor imprecision (number/share) · good vocabulary.

samples.text:
The charts compare the reasons international visitors gave for coming to a particular country in 2014 and 2024.

Leisure travel dominated in both years and became even more prevalent over the decade, whereas business travel declined dramatically. Educational visits, though still a small category, also grew substantially.

In 2014, holidays were the purpose of 44% of visits, with business trips a clear second at 28%. A further 18% of visitors came to see friends or relatives, while study and other reasons were marginal, at 5% each.

Ten years later, the proportion of holidaymakers had risen to 51%, meaning that just over half of all visitors were tourists. The most striking change, however, was in business travel, whose share was exactly halved to 14%, causing it to slip behind visits to friends and relatives, which rose modestly to 21%. Study, meanwhile, doubled its share to 10%, becoming a considerably more significant motive than before, and the residual category of other reasons remained negligible at 4%. Taken together, these changes indicate that the country's visitor profile became increasingly centred on personal rather than professional travel.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected with a clear overview · accurate figures used for precise comparison (halved, doubled) · sophisticated cohesion · wide, precise vocabulary · varied, error-free structures throughout.
